20: Direct integration: MAX to you
21: There are three ways you can get user-level revenue data:
22: User revenue API:
23: Use this API to retrieve user-level revenue data on a daily basis.
24: You can retrieve this data in two forms: aggregated for a particular user or with one row per impression.
25: Data is available eight hours after UTC day end.
26: Learn more on
27: the user revenue API documentation page
28: .
29: Client-side:
30: You can access impression-level user revenue data on the client side in real-time.
31: You can find integration instructions for
32: Android
33: and
34: iOS
35: in this documentation.
36: Server-to-server:
37: You can also access real-time revenue data on the server side.
38: To do this, provide an impression postback that tracks impression-level user ad revenue data.
39: Contact your account team or
40: the support team
41: to enable this feature.
42: This feature, and the macros that the impression postback supports, are described in
43: the “Server-to-server impression revenue API” section
44: of this page.
45: MMP integration: MAX to MMP
46: MAX has analytics partners who can help you access your data in a single dashboard.
47: You can work with any of AppLovin’s supported partners to access impression-level ad revenue or aggregated ad revenue data.
48: These supported partners include
49: Adjust
50: ,
51: GameAnalytics
52: ,
53: AppsFlyer
54: , and
55: Singular
56: .
57: Refer to the documentation pages maintained by those partners for more information about their capabilities.
58: Server-to-server impression revenue API
59: Contact your account team or
60: the support team
61: to enable this feature.
62: AppLovin’s servers can send postbacks to an external endpoint whenever they record a MAX impression.
63: You define which endpoint receives these requests.
64: The postbacks are in the form of HTTP or HTTPS
65: GET
66: requests.
67: AppLovin makes these postbacks soon after the impression, but they may be delayed by a few minutes.
68: You can use an impression timestamp macro to reconcile any delay between the impression and the postback times.
69: The postback request times-out if five seconds pass without a response from your endpoint.
70: There are no retries for postback requests.
71: Example
72: https://myimpressionserver.com/impression?idfa={IDFA}&user_id={USER_ID}&event={EVENT_ID}&token={EVENT_TOKEN}
73: Available macros
74: You can incorporate any of the macros in the following table into your postback URL.
75: The example URL above incorporates the
76: {IDFA}
77: ,
78: {USER_ID}
79: ,
80: {EVENT_ID}
81: , and
82: {EVENT_TOKEN}
83: macros.
84: AppLovin’s servers replace these macro names with accurate values when the servers make the request to your endpoint.
85: Name
86: Description
87: {AD_UNIT_ID}
88: MAX ad unit ID (16 hex characters)
89: Example:
90: 9ad0816ac071552a
91: {AD_UNIT_NAME}
92: Ad unit name (URL-encoded)
93: Example:
94: My%20App%20Banners
95: {AD_UNIT_TEST_NAME}
96: Name of the ad unit test, URL-encoded

98: Control
99: {ALL_REVENUE}
100: Estimated revenue, including FB Bidding estimates

103: ,

105: {CC}
106: Two-letter country code of the user
107: Example:
108: gb
109: {CUSTOM_DATA}
110: Custom data passed in from the integration (URL-encoded). AppLovin recommends that you keep the size of the string under 8192 characters. You must not include ampersand (
111: &
112: ) characters in the custom data if you include this macro.
113: Example:
114: my%20custom%20data
115: {DEVICE_TYPE}
116: User’s device type.
117: Example:
118: Tablet

120: Unique event ID, 36-character UUID
121: Example:
122: a7c3e1b2-4f59-4d8a-9c21-8e6b0f3a1d47

124: sha1( «event-ID» + «your-event-key» )

149: {IDFV}

153: {IP}

155: Examples:
156: 162.1.1.1
157: ,
158: fe80%3A%3A1ff%3Afe23%3A4567%3A890a%0A

161: Example:
162: APPLOVIN_NETWORK
163: {NETWORK_PLACEMENT}

165: Example:

12: > Pass post-install event data from your app to Unity Ads through an MMP to optimize user acquisition campaigns based on real user engagement, such as sessions, purchases, ad revenue, and level completions.
13: 
14: Unity Ads User Acquisition campaigns that are optimized for acquiring particular kinds of users, such as [Retention](/grow/acquire/campaigns/retention/retention-campaigns.md), [Return on Ad Spend](/grow/acquire/campaigns/roas/return-on-ad-spend-campaigns.md) (ROAS), and [Event](/grow/acquire/campaigns/event/event-campaigns.md) campaigns, require information about how users engage with your app after installing it. Post-install event data informs Unity's models to more accurately show ads to your campaign's target audience.
15: 
16: When you integrate with an MMP, you can enable your preferred partner to pass post-install event data to Unity. Each type of optimized campaign requires at least one type of post-install event data. However, you can pass data from all event types to any of your campaigns. The recommended best practice is to pass data for all post-install events because the additional data can improve your campaign performance.
17: 
18: Integrated partners can pass the following types of post-install event data:
19: 
20: | Post-install event | Description                                                           | Related campaigns                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
21: | ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
22: | Session            | Users open your app                                                   | [Retention](/grow/acquire/campaigns/retention/retention-campaigns.md)                                                                                                                                                              |
23: | Purchase           | Purchases users make in your app                                      | * [In-app Purchase (IAP) ROAS](/grow/acquire/campaigns/roas/purchase/in-app-purchase.md)
24: * [Hybrid ROAS](/grow/acquire/campaigns/roas/hybrid/hybrid.md)
25: * [Payer](/grow/acquire/campaigns/event/intro-to-event-campaigns.md#payer) |
26: | Ad revenue         | Revenue from ads that your users watch in your app                    | - [Ad Revenue ROAS](/grow/acquire/campaigns/roas/ad-revenue/ad-revenue.md)
27: - [Hybrid ROAS](/grow/acquire/campaigns/roas/hybrid/hybrid.md)                                                                                          |
28: | Level Complete     | A specific milestone or completion event your users reach in your app | [Level Complete](/grow/acquire/campaigns/event/intro-to-event-campaigns.md#level-complete)                                                                                                                                         |
29: 
30: > **Note:**
31: >
32: > To run an [Event optimization](/grow/acquire/campaigns/event/event-campaigns.md.md) campaign (Retention, Payer, or Level Complete), you must use one of the following MMPs:
33: >
34: > * Adjust
35: > * AppsFlyer
36: > * Singular
37: 
38: ## Supported post-install events
39: 
40: Most MMPs support passing post-install event data, usually through server postback URLs. To run optimized ad campaigns, use your preferred MMP's dashboard to set up post-install event passing.
41: 
42: > **Note:**
43: >
44: > Sharing some event data types might require additional subscriptions with your preferred MMP. Refer to the individual [Partner integration](/grow/acquire/partner-integration.md) guides in this documentation for information about your partner's requirements.
45: 
46: Refer to the following tables for which event types each of these common integrated partners support:
47: 
48: | **MMP**   | **Session** | **Purchase** | **Ad revenue** | **Level Complete** |
49: | --------- | ----------- | ------------ | -------------- | ------------------ |
50: | AppsFlyer | Yes         | Yes          | Yes            | Yes                |
51: | Adjust    | Yes         | Yes          | Yes            | Yes                |
52: | Singular  | Yes         | Yes          | Yes            | Yes                |
53: | Tenjin    | Yes         | Yes          | Yes            | No                 |
54: | Branch    | Yes         | Yes          | No             | No                 |
55: | Kochava   | Yes         | Yes          | No             | No                 |
56: 
57: > **Important:**
58: >
59: > Ensure that you carefully follow your attribution partner's integration instructions. Incorrect integrations will result in loss of event data because your servers can't retroactively send data from events.
